summary: Before the Deltan migration leaves its camp, a small pack of leopard-like predators, which Bob calls leopard-analogues, drags down a hunter who has strayed from the group; the other Deltans drive them off with spears, and he survives badly wounded. Bob tells Marvin he will help the Deltans for about a generation and then fade into legend so that they do not come to depend on him, and Marvin says that is roughly when he will leave to explore and meet other species. With a new batch of busters bringing his forces up to strength, Bob presents the resumption of the march to the circle of elders as information rather than an order, and after about a week of rest the tribe sets off the next morning without trouble. The second half of the trek is slower, through rougher, near-jungle country on the tropical south side of the mountains, so the migration will arrive well behind schedule, though winter is less of a concern there. Archimedes, now attached to a female from his cohort whom Bob calls Diana, agrees to introduce Bob to the tribe's medicine woman, whom he will not confront himself, and Diana insists on coming along. Three more gorilloid attacks, all smaller than the first raid, cost only a couple of lives against extensive gorilloid losses before the migration reaches the flint site. There Bob wants to thin out the gorilloids for miles around, while Marvin argues for killing only attackers so that the survivors learn to avoid the Deltans; Bob agrees to judge the situation at the site.

introducing.name: Diana
introducing.current_state: A female Deltan from Archimedes' cohort whom Bob calls Diana, recently attached to Archimedes. Clearly afraid of Bob, she still stays close to Archimedes and insists on joining Bob's planned visit to the medicine woman.

updates.current_state: At Delta Eridani, guarding the Deltan migration, which has resumed its march and reached the flint site after three smaller gorilloid attacks. He means to help the Deltans for about a generation and then fade into legend, and will judge at the site whether to thin out the local gorilloids.

At Delta Eridani with Bob, with a batch of new Bobs under way at the autofactory, he argues for killing only gorilloids that attack the Deltans rather than hunting them out around the flint site. He expects to leave in about a generation to explore and meet other species.

Effectively a member of the tribal council and recently attached to Diana, he travels with the migration on its second leg. He trusts Bob's ideas but will not confront the tribe's medicine woman, and has agreed to introduce Bob to her.

updates.description: An intelligent native population of Delta Eridani 4, named Deltans by Bob. Bob judges them to be fire-using and probably intelligent. They have bat- and pig-like faces, long spiderish limbs, light brownish-gray to orangey-tan fur, patterned heads, and mobile expressive ears; ears pointing straight down are their equivalent of an incredulous stare. Their language is far more guttural than any sound humans can produce. Bob observes six apparently friendly groups, each tending a fire and interacting with the others. He observes two genders, tribal organization, loose pairings, and some individuals with multiple significant others; males patrol their territory while females and children form the tribe's center, and tribal matters are put before a council of elders, while juveniles have lower standing. Bob regards them as a decisive people who, when action is required, carry out orders without argument. They have an annual breeding cycle. Marvin finds no concept of religion among them, only basic animism such as honoring the animals they kill for food and venerating their dead. A planetary survey finds Deltans on only one continent of Eden, their cradle, making them a strictly local mutation; many related species live there, but none use fire or make tools. Their traditional weapons are clubs, handheld rocks, and pointed sticks, and axes and spears are now in use. A small tribal population with a small gene pool is under pressure from larger, stronger gorilloid predators, and Bob's group helps them regain flintworking, learn to preserve meat, and improve their defenses. The tribe once lived in older villages, some with flint, a better water supply, more food, and better defenses, before being driven out. Their medicine, overseen in the tribe by a medicine woman, is at a potion-and-poultice stage, and Bob doubts it can mend injuries such as a broken leg.

The fourth inner rocky planet in the Delta Eridani system, also called Delta Eridani 4 and DE-4. It is slightly larger than Earth, with lower surface gravity, a somewhat denser atmosphere, and conditions that support soaring flyers and tall tree analogues. Its observed temperate-to-subtropical landscape has meadows, rocky bluffs, and forest-like expanses of exceptionally large brownish trees with wide horizontal branches and thick leaf canopies. Documented wildlife includes six-legged exoskeletal insect analogues, small furry six-legged mammal analogues, larger four-limbed mammal analogues, feather-like bird analogues, and a three-segment mammalian snake equivalent. One four-legged winged variant, provisionally called a hippogriff by Bob, shows limited color-change camouflage. Bob, Marvin, Luke, and Bender adopt Eden as the world name associated with the Deltans' birthplace. A mountainous spine runs down the center of the Deltans' home continent, and only a couple of its passes are low enough to be useful. Its ecosystem is as full and diverse as Earth's, with more than one apex predator, among them pack-hunting leopard-like predators, which Bob calls leopard-analogues, that kill with a suffocating death grip.
